topic: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900) certification exam preparation - refreshed for the January 2026 exam update
exam_format: 40-60 questions, 45 minutes (65 minutes total seat time), passing score 700/1000, online proctored or test center. Question types include multiple choice, multiple select, drag-and-drop, and hot area. No prerequisites; certification does not expire.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple select clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE'
audience: Complete beginners to cloud computing, business stakeholders, sales and procurement professionals, and career changers who want to validate foundational Azure knowledge. No technical background required.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Describe cloud concepts
domains.notes: Cloud computing definition, shared responsibility model, public/private/hybrid cloud, consumption-based model and cloud pricing, comparing IaaS/PaaS/SaaS and appropriate use cases, benefits of high availability, scalability, reliability, predictability, security, governance, and manageability in the cloud.

domains.name: Describe Azure architecture and services
domains.notes: Core architectural components: regions, region pairs, sovereign regions, availability zones, datacenters, resources and resource groups, subscriptions, management groups. Compute: VMs, VM scale sets, availability sets, Azure Virtual Desktop, containers, Azure Container Instances, AKS, Azure Functions, App Service. Networking: virtual networks, subnets, peering, DNS, VPN Gateway, ExpressRoute, public/private endpoints. Storage: storage services, tiers, redundancy options, storage account options, file movement (AzCopy, Storage Explorer, File Sync), migration options (Azure Migrate, Data Box). Identity/access/security: Microsoft Entra ID, authentication methods (SSO, MFA, passwordless), external identities, Conditional Access, RBAC, Zero Trust, defense-in-depth, Microsoft Defender for Cloud. JANUARY 2026 UPDATE: expanded coverage of Azure AI services - Azure OpenAI in Foundry Models, Azure AI services overview, Microsoft Copilot family, and responsible AI principles - now appears in this domain and is heavily tested.

domains.name: Describe Azure management and governance
domains.notes: Cost management: factors affecting costs, pricing calculator vs TCO calculator, Microsoft Cost Management, tags. Governance and compliance: Microsoft Purview, Azure Policy, resource locks. Resource management tools: Azure portal, Cloud Shell, Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell, Azure Arc, IaC concepts, ARM templates/Bicep. Monitoring: Azure Advisor, Azure Service Health, Azure Monitor (Log Analytics, alerts, Application Insights). JANUARY 2026 UPDATE: governance and cost management weighting increased - this domain is now co-equal with architecture in practice; expect more scenario questions on cost optimization and policy enforcement.

extra_guidance: This is a REFRESHED 2026 EDITION of an existing TechNuggets course - the marketing angle is 'fully refreshed for the January 14, 2026 exam update', because candidates studying from pre-2025 materials report being surprised by AI questions. The three domain names and weights above are Microsoft's official skills-measured outline - use them verbatim. Give genuine weight to the January 2026 additions: Azure AI services, Azure OpenAI, Microsoft Copilot, and responsible AI principles woven through the architecture domain, plus the heavier governance/cost emphasis. This is a fundamentals exam for a NON-TECHNICAL audience - explain every acronym on first use, use business-scenario framing ('your company wants to...'), and avoid code-heavy labs. Labs should be portal-based explorations: navigate the pricing calculator, create a resource group with tags, explore Entra ID, review Azure Advisor recommendations - all doable on a free account. Include drag-and-drop and multiple-select question styles in practice tests since the real exam uses them. Cover the classic exam traps: region pair vs availability zone, IaaS/PaaS/SaaS boundary cases (e.g. SQL on VM vs Azure SQL), TCO vs pricing calculator, Policy vs RBAC vs locks, Advisor vs Monitor vs Service Health. Final chapter must be a full exam simulation walkthrough with 45-minute time-management strategy.
